pr_title: SingleThreadedEventLoop: add read-only iterator of channels
pr_body:
Motivation:

For servers there is a need for per eventloop "watchdog" timer that ticks for all eventloop channels. For moderately high number of connections, It is cheaper cpu-wise than per channel scheduling.

Now this requires additional data structure to hold active channels - which is wasteful as It duplicates the one from SingleThreadedEventLoop (its practically useful impls - epoll, kqueue, nio).

Modification:

Add read-only iterator of eventloop channels exposed on SingleThreadedEventLoop as 
`Iterator<Channel> registeredChannelsIterator()`.

Result:

SingleThreadedEventLoop channels may be iterated without additional redundant data structures.

Fixes #12595.
pr_comments: We also have `AbstractSingleThreadEventLoopTest` which covers epoll and kqueue. I don't know why nio hasn't been migrated to using that.

### Expected behavior

For servers there is a need for per eventloop "watchdog" timer that ticks for all eventloop channels. For moderately high number of connections, It is cheaper cpu-wise than per channel scheduling. 

Now this requires additional data structure to hold active channels - which is wasteful as It duplicates the one from `SingleThreadedEventLoop` (its practically useful impls - epoll, kqueue, nio). 

It would be convenient to avoid this redundant additional data structure, and instead have read-only iterator of eventloop channels exposed on `SingleThreadedEventLoop` as `Iterator<Channel> registeredChannelsIterator()` (complementary to existing `int registeredChannels()` for channels count).

comments: `NioEventLoop` do not already have a channel map, even though it knows how many channels are registered.

@chrisvest `NioEventLoop` has all its channels as collection - `selector.keys()`, where each key has ref to `NioChannel` with `attachment()`. While not map but collection, It also may be iterated the same way as `Map.values()`. Anyways, I replaced all `map`s to `data structure` in issue description.

In that case I think it's fine to add if we mention in the javadoc that the method is optional, and the default implementation throws UnsupportedOperationException.

Are you interested in providing a PR?
I created a pr. please review.

review_comments: I think this is not thread-safe as calling values() is not thread-safe
I think this is not thread-safe as calling values() is not thread-safe

It is intended to be non-thread-safe, and be called from within event loop only (same as its `int registeredChannels()` sibling). Do you have use-case in mind? IMO thread-safe channels iterator would make sense for `EventLoopGroup` and not individual event loops.

On the other hand, in tests iterator is incorrectly used outside of eventloop so that needs to be fixed.
@mostroverkhov in this case we should check `inEventLoop()` and if not throw.
Add to the docs that this is only expected to be called from within  the event loop.
How about adding some javadoc and marking it `@UnstableApi`?
